chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام.
That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, when the male animal charged the first time, he did not hold its owner liable; but when it did so a second time, he held its owner liable.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, the authority from whom this legal ruling is reported
key_terms.الْفَحْلُ: the male animal, especially a breeding male
key_terms.ضَمَّنَ: he held liable or made responsible

ai.seo_question: When is an animal owner liable if the animal attacks someone in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning liability for harm caused by an animal. It indicates that the owner is not held liable the first time the animal attacks, but liability is imposed after repeated behavior, showing consideration of prior knowledge and responsibility.
